42:1: We have mentioned the differences among the people of interpretation regarding the meanings of the letters of the alphabet with which the first chapters of the Qur’an begin, and we have shown what is correct in our view of what they say about that with evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place, since these letters are similar to the previous ones. We have mentioned a statement from Hudhayfah regarding the meaning of this in particular, which is: Ahmad bin Zuhair narrated to us, saying: Abdul Wahhab bin Najdah Al-Hawti narrated to us, saying: Abu Al-Mughira Abdul Quddus bin Al-Hajjaj Al-Himsi narrated to us, on the authority of Arta’ah bin Al-Mundhir, who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said to him, while Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman was with him: Tell me the interpretation of the words of God, Ha Meem * Ain Sin Qaf. He said: So he lowered his head and turned away from him. Then he repeated his words and he turned away but did not answer him at all and disliked his words. Then he repeated them a third time but did not answer him at all, so Hudhayfah said to him: I will tell you about it, you know why he disliked it. It was revealed about a man from his family called Abdul-Ilah or Abdullah, who will descend upon a river from the rivers of the East. Two cities will be built on it, and the river will split between them, black and dark, and burned, as if it had never been in its place. Its inhabitants will wake up wondering how they escaped, but it will be no more than the whiteness of that day until every tyrant gathers around them, then God will cause the earth to swallow them and them all. So that is His words, Ha Meem * Ain Sin Qaf, meaning: a decree from God, a trial and a judgment. Ham Ain means fair, Seen means will be, and Qaf means located in these two cities. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to read it <Ha Mim * Saq>without an ‘ayn, and he said: The seen represents the life of every existing sect and the qaf represents every existing group, and he said: Ali only knew the ‘ayn by it. It was mentioned that this is in the copy of Abdullah in the same way as what was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his reading it without an ‘ayn.
42:3: And His statement: Thus does He reveal to you and to those before you, God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. God Almighty says: Thus does He reveal to you, O Muhammad, and to those of His prophets before you. It was said that Ha Mim Ain Seen Qaf was revealed to every prophet sent, just as it was revealed to our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Therefore it was said: Thus does He reveal to you and to those before you, God, the Exalted in Might, in His vengeance against His enemies, the Wise in His management of His creation.
42:4: God Almighty says: To God belongs the kingdom of whatever is in the heavens and what is on the earth of all things and He is the Most High meaning: He is high and lofty over everything, and all things are below Him, because they are under His authority, His power is in effect over them, and His will is not lost in them the Great who has greatness, pride, and dominance.
42:5: And His saying: The heavens almost burst from above them means that the Almighty says: The heavens almost burst from above the earth, from the greatness and majesty of the Most Merciful. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: The heavens almost burst from above them he said: He means from the weight and greatness of the Most Gracious, Blessed and Exalted be He. Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: The heavens almost burst from above them means from the greatness and majesty of God. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, The heavens almost burst. He said: They split in His statement, Broken by it (al-Muzzammil 73:18). He said: Split by it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Regarding His statement: They burst from above them he said: They crack from the majesty of God. Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi narrated: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Abu Ma`shar from Muhammad ibn Qays who said: A man came to Ka`b and said: O Ka`b, where is our Lord? The people said to him: God is insignificant! Do you ask about this? Ka`b said: Leave him, for if he is knowledgeable he will increase, and if he is ignorant you will learn. I asked where our Lord is, and He is reclining on the Mighty Throne, with one leg placed on the other. The distance of this earth that you are on is five hundred years, and from earth to earth is a journey of five hundred years, and its density is five hundred years, until seven earths are completed. Then from earth to heaven is a journey of five hundred years, and its density is five hundred years, and God is reclining on the Throne. Then the heavens will burst. Ka`b then said: Recite if you wish: The heavens almost burst from above them... the verse. And His statement: And the angels glorify the praises of their Lord, God Almighty says: And the angels pray in obedience to their Lord and in gratitude to Him out of awe of His majesty and greatness. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the angels glorify the praises of their Lord. He said: And the angels glorify Him out of His greatness. His statement: And they ask forgiveness for those on earth means: And they ask their Lord to forgive the sins of those on earth who believe in Him. As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And they ask forgiveness for those on earth, he said: For the believers. God Almighty says: Behold, God is the Forgiving of the sins of His believing servants, the Most Merciful towards them, that He does not punish them after they have repented from them.
42:6: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And those who have taken, O Muhammad, of the polytheists of your people, besides God, gods to be their guardians and worship, God is a Guardian over them, He keeps track of their deeds and records their actions in order to recompense them for them on the Day of Resurrection, and you are not a guardian over them.” He says: You, O Muhammad, are not a guardian over them in recording their deeds, but you are only a warner, so convey to them what you were sent with, for upon you is only the conveyance and upon us is the reckoning.
42:7: God Almighty says: Thus, We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, an Arabic Qur’an, in the language of the Arabs, because those to whom I sent you were Arabs, so We revealed this Qur’an to you in their languages, so that they would understand what it contains of God’s proofs and His remembrance, because We do not send a messenger except with the language of his people, to explain to them so that you may warn the Mother of Cities, which is Mecca, and those around it, meaning: and those around the Mother of Cities from among all the people. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: To warn the Mother of Cities, he said: Mecca. And His statement: And warn of the Day of Assembly, meaning, the Almighty says: And warn of God’s punishment on the Day of Assembly of His servants for the standing place of reckoning and presentation. It was also said: And warn of the Day of Assembly, meaning: And warn them on the Day of Assembly, just as it was said: He frightens His allies, meaning: He frightens you, His allies. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And warn of the Day of Assembly, he said: the Day of Resurrection. His saying: There is no doubt about it means: There is no doubt about it. His statement: A group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze means: Among them is a group in Paradise, and they are those who believed in God and followed what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought them. And a group in the Blaze means: Among them is a group in the blazing fire of God upon its people, and they are those who disbelieved in God and disobeyed what His Messenger brought them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Abu Qabil al-Ma’afiri, on the authority of Shafi al-Asbahi, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us with two books in his hand and said: Do you know what this is? We said: No, unless you tell us, O Messenger of God. He said: This is a book from the Lord of the Worlds, in it are the names of the people of Paradise, the names of their fathers and their tribes - then he summarized them at the end of them - so nothing will ever be added to them or taken away from them. And this is the book of the people of Hellfire with their names and the names of their fathers - then he summarized them at the end of them - so nothing will ever be added to them or taken away from them. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So what should we do if this is a matter that has been completed? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, strive hard and come close, for the inhabitant of Paradise will be sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise, no matter what deeds he does, and the inhabitant of Hellfire will be sealed with the deeds of Hellfire, no matter what deeds he does. Your Lord has completed His servants. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said with his hands and threw them away: He has completed. Your Lord is from among the creation, a group in Paradise, and a group in the Blaze. They said: Glory be to God, so why do we work and strive? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Works last until their conclusion. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith and Haywah ibn Shuraih told me, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Asid, that Abu Firas told him that he heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: When God, the Exalted, created Adam, He shook him as one shakes a bag, and brought forth from him every offspring, and out came those like the thorns. He took them in two handfuls, then said: The wretched and the blessed. Then He cast them down, then He took them and said: A group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze. He said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, on the authority of Abu Shabwayh, who told him on the authority of Ibn Hujaira that it had reached him that Moses said: “O Lord, You created those whom You created. You made a group of them in Paradise and a group in the Blaze. If You did not admit them all into Paradise, He said: O Moses, raise your crops. So they were raised. He said: I have been raised. He said: Raise them. So he raised them, and did not leave anything. He said: O Lord, I have been raised. He said: Raise them. He said: I have been raised, except for that which is not good. He said: Thus, I admit all of My creation into Paradise, except for that which is not good.” And it was said: A group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze, so it was raised. The discussion had already been presented before that with His statement: To warn the Mother of Cities and those around it, in the accusative case, because it was intended to be the beginning, just as one says: I saw the army killed or defeated, meaning: some of them were killed, and some of them were defeated.
42:8: God Almighty says: And if God had wanted to unite His creation upon guidance, and make them upon one religion, He would have done so, and He would have made them one nation: meaning: people of one religion, and a group united upon one faith. But He admits whom He wills into His mercy. He says: He did not do that and make them one nation, but He admits whom He wills of His servants into His mercy, meaning that He admits them into His mercy by enabling them to enter into His religion, with which He sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the wrongdoers will have neither protector nor helper. He says: And the disbelievers in God will have neither a protector nor a helper to defend them from God’s punishment when He punishes them, saving them from His torment, and exacting retribution for them from those whom He punished. This was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to console him for the worry he was experiencing due to his people turning away from him, and to command him to refrain from causing harm to himself because of the turning away of those who turned away from him and did not respond to the truth he called him to, and to inform him that the affairs of His servants are in His hand, and that He is the guide to the truth whomever He wills, and the misguider whomever He wills, apart from Him and apart from everyone else.
42:9: God Almighty says: Or have these polytheists taken allies besides God to be their allies? God is the ally. He says: God is the ally of His allies, and let them take Him as a ally, not gods and idols, nor that which has no power to harm or benefit them. And He gives life to the dead. He says: God gives life to the dead after their death, and He will gather them on the Day of Resurrection. And He is over all things competent. He says: God is able to give life to His creation after their death and to do so over others, for He is capable of all things.
42:10: And His statement: And whatever you differ over, its judgment is with God. God Almighty says: And whatever you differ over, O people, and dispute among yourselves, its judgment is with God. He says: For God is the One who judges between you and sets forth the ruling regarding it. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And whatever you differ over, its ruling is with God, Ibn Amr said in his hadith: He judges it, and Al-Harith said: God judges it. And His statement: That is God, my Lord, in Him I have relied, means that He is saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to these polytheists that this one, whose attributes these are, is my Lord, not your gods that you call upon besides Him, who have no power over anything. In Him I have relied in my affairs, and to Him I have entrusted my means, and in Him I have put my trust. And to Him I turn, means: and to Him I return in my affairs and repent for my sins.
42:11: God Almighty says: The Creator of the heavens and the earth, the Creator of the seven heavens and the earth. As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, his statement: Creator of the heavens and the earth he said: Creator. And His statement: And He has made for you mates from among yourselves means, the Most High says: Your Lord has made you mates from among yourselves. And He, the Most High, said from among yourselves because He created Eve from Adam’s rib, so he is from the men. And from the livestock, mates means, the Most High says: And He has made for you mates from among the livestock, two from the sheep, two from the goats, two from the camels, two from the cows, males and females, and from every kind of that. He multiplies you therein means He creates you from what He has made for you from your mates, and He gives you life from what He has made for you from the livestock. The commentators differed on the meaning of His statement: He creates you therein in this context. Some of them said: The meaning of this is that He creates you therein. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: He scatters you therein, he said: Generation after generation of people and livestock. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, his statement: He creates you, he said: He creates you. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: He will cause you to scatter therein, he said: generation after generation of people and livestock. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, that he said regarding this verse, He creates you therein, that is, He creates you. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: He makes you live in it. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: He has made for you mates from among yourselves and mates from the livestock, multiplying you therein means: He makes for you a livelihood in it by which you live. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: He scatters you therein. He said: He makes you live therein. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa`id told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, He scatters you therein, he said: Sustenance from God through which He sustains you. Although these two statements differ in wording from their speakers, they may be interpreted as having the same meaning, which is that the speaker means by He sustains you therein, meaning: He gives you life through your living therein, just as He gives life to one who was not created by forming him and breathing life into him until he lives. The meaning of God scatters the creation has been explained previously with sufficient evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. His saying: There is nothing like Him has two meanings: One of them is that it means: He is not like anything, and the word like was introduced into the speech to emphasize the speech if the wording differs with it and with the letter kaf, and they have one meaning, as was said. Once you are called something you hate Then add to <ma>, which is a letter of denial, <in>, which is also a letter of denial, because the pronunciation is different between them, even though their meanings are the same, to emphasize the speech, as Aws ibn Hajar said: My dead are like palm trunks covered with pouring rain. Meaning: like palm trunks, and as the other said: Saad bin Zaid: If you see their virtue, there is no one like them among the people. The other: that its meaning is: There is nothing like Him, and the kaf is the one that enters into the speech, like the rajaz poet’s saying: And the prayers are as if they are influential So he added a kaf to the kaf to emphasize the comparison, as the other said: The ghadaiq on the road is smaller than an egg in a sieve So he inserted the kaf with <about>, and we have explained this in a place other than this one with an explanation that is more eloquent than this explanation, so we made a concession in explaining it in this place. And His statement: And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, He, the Most High, says, describing Himself with what He is, and He means Himself: The All-Hearing of what His creation utters, the All-Seeing of their deeds. Nothing of that is hidden from Him, and nothing of it escapes His knowledge. He encompasses all of it, examining its small and great things. That every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned (al-Jathiyah 45:22) of good or evil.
42:12: He, the Most High, means by His saying: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth, that He has the keys to the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, and in His hand are the locks and keys of good and evil. Whatever mercy He opens, none can withhold it, and whatever mercy He withholds, none can release it after Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, He has the keys of the heavens and the earth. He said: Keys in Persian. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: He has the keys to the heavens and the earth. He said: The keys to the heavens and the earth. And similarly, on the authority of al-Hasan. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: He has the keys to the heavens and the earth. He said: The treasuries of the heavens and the earth. And His statement: He expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it means: He expands His provision and His grace for whom He wills of His creation, and He expands it for him, and increases his wealth and makes him rich. And He restricts: and He is stingy for whom He wills of them, so He makes him tight and impoverishes him. Indeed, He is Knowing of all things means: God, the Blessed and Exalted, is aware of everything He does of His expansion for whom He expands, and His restriction for whom He restricts, and who of His creation is better for whom He corrupts in provision, and who is better for whom He restricts and corrupts, and other matters. He is All-Knowing, and nothing is hidden from Him regarding expansion and restriction and other matters of the good management of His creation. God Almighty says: “So to Him who has the keys of the heavens and the earth, whose description is as I have described to you in these verses, O people, so long for Him, and worship Him, devoting your religion to Him alone, not to idols, gods, and statues, which have no power to harm or benefit you.”
42:13: God Almighty says: Your Lord has ordained for you, O people, of the religion that which He enjoined upon Noah to do, and that which We have revealed to you, meaning to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: “And He has ordained for you of the religion which We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, and We have commanded you with it, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus - to establish the religion.” He says: He has ordained for you of the religion, that you establish the religion. So if that is the meaning of the statement, it is in the accusative case as a translation of what in His statement: what He enjoined upon Noah. It is also permissible for it to be in the genitive case in response to the ha’ in His statement: with it, and as an explanation of it, so the meaning of the statement in that case would be: He has ordained for you of the religion that which He enjoined upon Noah, that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein. It is also permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a new sentence, so the meaning of the statement in that case would be: He has ordained for you of the religion that which He enjoined, which is that you establish the religion. Since the meaning of the words is what I have described, it is known that what all these prophets recommended was one recommendation, which is to establish the true religion, and not to be divided in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: What He enjoined upon Noah he said: What He enjoined upon you and His prophets, all of them are one religion. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah, he said: It is the entire religion. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah Noah was sent when he was sent with the law to make permissible what is permissible and to forbid what is forbidden, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah. He said: What is lawful and what is unlawful. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah... to the end of the verse. He said: What has been said to you is sufficient for you. What he meant by his saying: Establish the religion is that you should act according to what was prescribed and imposed for you, as we have explained previously in his saying: Establish the prayer. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: Establish the religion, he said: Work according to it. His statement: And do not be divided therein means: Do not differ in the religion that you have been commanded to uphold, as the parties differed before you. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And do not be divided therein means that division is destruction, and that the group is trustworthy. And His statement: It is difficult for the polytheists what you call them to, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: It is difficult for the polytheists among your people, O Muhammad, what you call them to of sincere worship of God, singling Him out as divinity, and disavowing all other gods and rivals besides Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, The polytheists found what you are calling them to difficult. He said: The polytheists rejected it, and the testimony that there is no god but God was difficult for them, so Satan and his soldiers confronted it, but God, the Blessed and Exalted, refused to do anything except carry it out, support it, triumph over it, and make it prevail over those who opposed it. And His saying: God chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back means: God chooses for Himself whomever He wills from among His creation, and chooses for Himself and His guardianship whomever He loves. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: God chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him], meaning: He guides to work in obedience to Him and follows the truth with which He sent His Prophet, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, whoever turns to His obedience and repents from His sins. As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And He guides to Him whoever turns back: whoever turns to obeying God.
42:14: God Almighty says: The polytheists did not become divided in their religions and become parties except after knowledge had come to them that what God had commanded them to do, and with which He had sent Noah, was to establish the true religion, and that you should not become divided therein. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them. So he said: Beware of division, for it is destruction. Out of envy among themselves. He says: Out of envy and hostility from some of you against others for the sake of worldly gain. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term. God Almighty says: And had it not been for a word that preceded, O Muhammad, from your Lord, He would not have hastened the punishment upon them, but He delayed it until a specified term, and that specified term, as He mentioned, is the Day of Resurrection. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term, he said: the Day of Resurrection. His statement: It will be judged between them means: Your Lord will finish judging between these people who differed about the truth with which He sent His Prophet Noah after they had learned about it, by destroying the people of falsehood among them and making the people of truth prevail over them. And His statement: And those who inherited the Scripture after them means: And those to whom God gave His Book, the Torah and the Gospel, after these people who differed about the truth, are in disquieting doubt about it means: They are in disquieting doubt about the religion that God enjoined upon Noah, and revealed to you, O Muhammad, and commanded you to establish. In a similar vein to what we said about the meaning of his statement: And those who inherited the Scripture after them, he said: The people of interpretation. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, his statement: And those who inherited the Scripture after them he said: The Jews and the Christians.
42:15: God the Most High says: “Then to that religion which He has ordained for you, and which He enjoined upon Noah, and which He revealed to you, O Muhammad. So call the servants of God, and be steadfast in acting upon it, and do not deviate from it, and remain steadfast upon it as your Lord has commanded you to be steadfast.” It was also said: Therefore, call, and the meaning is: Then to that, so the lam was used in place of ila, as it was said: Because your Lord has revealed it (Al-Zalzalah 95:5). We have explained that in more than one place in this book of ours. Some Arab scholars interpreted the meaning of the verse, So call to that to mean this, and said: The meaning of the statement is: So call to this Qur’an and be steadfast. The one who said this statement is close in meaning to what we have said, except that what we have said in it is more deserving of an interpretation of the statement, because it is in the context of God’s statement, may He be glorified and exalted, about what He has prescribed for you of the religion for His Prophet Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, to establish, and nothing has come in the statement that indicates that He has diverted from it to something else. And His statement: And do not follow their desires means, the Most High says: And do not, O Muhammad, follow the desires of those who doubted the truth that God has prescribed for you from among those who inherited the Book after the previous generations before them, so that you doubt it as those who doubted it, And say, ‘I believe in what God has revealed of the Book’ means, the Most High says: And say to them, O Muhammad, I believe in what God has revealed of the Book, whatever that Book may be, whether it is the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, or the Scrolls of Abraham. I do not deny any of it as you, O group of parties, deny some of it and believe in some of it. And His statement: And I have been commanded to be just among you - God, our Lord and your Lord - God Almighty says: And say to them, O Muhammad: My Lord has commanded me to be just among you, O group of parties, so I will walk among you all with the truth that He has commanded me with and sent me to call to it. Like what Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And I have been commanded to be just between you, he said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to be just, so he was just until he died, may God bless him and grant him peace. Justice is God’s scale on earth, by which He takes for the oppressed from the oppressor, and for the weak from the strong. By justice God confirms the truthful and denies the liar, and by justice He repels and rebukes the aggressor. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, David, peace be upon him, used to say: “There are three things that I greatly admire if someone has them: moderation in poverty and in wealth, justice in pleasure and in anger, and fear of God in secret and in public. And three things that whoever has them will destroy him: greed that is obeyed and followed, and self-admiration. And four things, whoever is given them has been given the best of this world and the next: a tongue that remembers, a grateful heart, a patient body, and a believing wife.” The Arab scholars differed over the meaning of the lam in his statement, And I was commanded to be just between you. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Its meaning is: so that, and I was commanded so that I may be just. Another said: The meaning of the statement is: And I was commanded to be just, and the command applies to what follows it, and the lam in la’adl is not a condition. He said: And I was commanded applies to an and kay and the lam, I was commanded that I worship, and so that I worship, and for worship. He said: And so is everything that requires the future tense, so it has these three aspects. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that the command is an agent in the meaning of to be just, because its meaning is: I have commanded justice among you. And His statement: God is our Lord and your Lord means: God is our Master and your Master, O group of parties from the People of the Two Books, the Torah and the Gospel. For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds means: For us is the reward for what we have acquired of deeds, and for you is the reward for what you have acquired of them. His saying: There is no argument between us and you means: There is no dispute between us and you. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: There is no argument between us and you, he said: There is no dispute. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God Almighty, There is no argument between us and you, there is no dispute between us and you, and he recited, And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best (al-Ankabut 29:46)... to the end of the verse. His saying: God will gather us together means: God will gather us together on the Day of Resurrection, and He will judge between us with justice in what we differed over. And to Him is the final destination means: And to Him is the return and recourse after our death.
42:16: God Almighty says: And those who dispute about the religion of God with which He sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the people had responded to him and entered into it, from among those who were given the Scripture, their argument is invalid meaning: Their dispute that they dispute about is false and lost before their Lord. And upon them is wrath meaning: Upon them is wrath from God, and for them in the Hereafter is a severe punishment, which is the punishment of the Fire. He mentioned that this verse was revealed about a group of Jews who disputed with the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about their religion, and they hoped to turn them away from it and turn them away from Islam to disbelief. Mentioning the narration from the one who mentioned that about him: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: And those who dispute about God after He has been responded to - their argument is worthless with their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment. He said: They are the People of the Book who used to dispute with the Muslims and turn them away from guidance after they had responded to God. He said: They are the people of misguidance who had been responded to despite their misguidance, and they were waiting for ignorance to come to them. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And those who dispute about God after He has been answered he said: Men hoped that ignorance would return. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said regarding this verse, And those who dispute about God after He has been answered, he said: After the people entered Islam. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And those who dispute about God after He has been answered - their argument is worthless before their Lord. He said: They are the Jews and Christians. They said: Our book came before your book, and our prophet came before your prophet, and we are better than you. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And those who dispute about God after He has been answered - their argument is worthless... the verse. He said: They are the Jews and Christians who disputed with the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: Our book came before your book, and our prophet came before your prophet, and we are closer to God than you. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And those who dispute about God... to the end of the verse, he said: He forbade him from disputing.
42:17: God Almighty says: God is He who sent down this Book meaning the Qur’an in truth and the Balance meaning: And He sent down the Balance, which is justice, to judge between people with fairness, and rule over them with the ruling of God that He commanded in His Book. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told us, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: He sent down the Book with the truth and the balance, he said: justice. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: Who sent down the Book with the truth and the Balance, he said: The Balance means justice. And His saying: And what makes you know that perhaps the Hour is near? God Almighty says: And what makes you know and teaches you that perhaps the Hour in which the Resurrection will take place is near.
42:18: Those who do not believe in it urge it on: He says: Those who are not certain of its coming urge you, O Muhammad, to hasten its coming, thinking that it will not come. And those who believe are fearful of it: He says: And those who believed in its coming and God’s promise to them that they would be gathered in it. are fearful of it: He says: And they are apprehensive of its coming, afraid of its occurrence, because they do not know what God will do to them in it. And they know that it is the truth: He says: And they are certain that its coming is the certain truth, they do not doubt its coming. Unquestionably, those who dispute about the Hour: God Almighty says: Unquestionably, those who dispute about the occurrence of the Hour and argue about it are in extreme error: He says: In injustice, far from the path of guidance, and deviating from the path of truth and right guidance, far from the truth.
42:19: God Almighty says: God is full of kindness to His servants. He provides for whomever He wills, giving him plenty and restricting whomever He wills among them. And He is the Strong whom no one can overcome due to His strength, and no one can resist Him if He wants to punish him with His power. The Mighty in His vengeance when He takes vengeance on those who disobey Him.
42:20: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest. God Almighty says: Whoever desires the Hereafter by his deeds, We increase for him in his harvest. He says: We increase for him his good deeds, so We give him ten for one, up to whatever increase our Lord wills. And whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him thereof. He says: And he did not desire the world by his deeds, striving for it, not for the Hereafter. We give him thereof what We have allotted for him. And he will have no share in the Hereafter. He says: And whoever seeks the world by his deeds, and God does not intend by them a share in the reward of God for the people of deeds that they desired with their deeds in this world. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We will increase for him his harvest... to and he will have no share in the Hereafter he said: He says: Whoever only works for this world, We will give him some of it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We increase for him in his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world”... the verse, he says: Whoever prefers his worldly life over his Hereafter - We will not give him a share in the Hereafter except the Fire, and We will not increase him in anything from this world except a provision that has already been completed and allotted to him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We increase for him in his harvest, he said: Whoever desires the Hereafter and its deeds, We increase for him in his deeds. And whoever desires the harvest of this world - We give him thereof,... to the end of the verse. He said: Whoever desires this world and its deeds, We give him thereof, and We do not make for him in the Hereafter a share of the harvest of deeds. Whoever works for the Hereafter, God gives him, and whoever works for this world, God gives him. Muhammad told me, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We will increase for him his harvest, he said: Whoever desires the work of the Hereafter - We will increase for him his work. And his saying: And he will have no share in the Hereafter, he said: The disbeliever will have a painful punishment.
42:21: God Almighty says: Or do these polytheists have partners in their polytheism and misguidance? They have instituted for them a religion which God has not permitted. He says: They have innovated for them a religion which God has not permitted them to innovate. And were it not for the decisive word, the judgment would have been passed between them. God Almighty says: And were it not for God’s previous command that He will not hasten their punishment in this world, and that He has already said that they will be delayed in punishment until the Day of Resurrection, the judgment between you and them would have been concluded by our hastening their punishment in this world. But for them in the Hereafter is a painful punishment, as God Almighty said: And indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment. He says: And indeed, for the disbelievers in God on the Day of Resurrection is a painful, agonizing punishment.
42:22: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: You will see, O Muhammad, the unbelievers in God on the Day of Resurrection, fearful of what they have earned. He says: fearful and afraid of God’s punishment for what they have earned in this world from their evil deeds. “Which is about to befall them.” He says: And those who are fearful of it, of God’s punishment descending upon them, and they will taste it without fail. And His statement: And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise, meaning: And those who believe in God and obey Him in what He commands and forbids in this world will be in the gardens of orchards in the Hereafter. What is meant by gardens is the plural of rawdah, which is a place that has abundant vegetation. The Arabs do not say gardens for places with trees. From this is the saying of Abu al-Najm: And the mangy one is like the one who has defiled the gardens of the meadow that have not been defiled By garden is meant the plural of garden. What God Almighty meant by that was the report of the joy and bliss they are experiencing. Muhammad ibn Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise to the end of the verse. He said: in the gardens of Paradise and its delights. And His statement: They will have whatever they wish with their Lord means that those who believe and do righteous deeds will have with their Lord in the Hereafter whatever their souls desire and their eyes delight in. That is the great bounty means, the Most High says: This which God has given them of this bliss and this honor in the Hereafter is the great bounty from God upon them, which makes every bliss and honor in this world superior to every other.
42:23: God Almighty says: This is what I have informed you of, O people, that I have prepared for those who believe and do righteous deeds in the Hereafter of bliss and honor, the good tidings that God gives to His servants who believed in Him in this world and worked in obedience to Him therein. Say, ‘I do not ask of you for this any reward.’ God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those of your people who dispute with you about the Hour: I do not ask of you, O people, for calling you to what I call you to of the truth that I have brought you, and the advice that I advise you, any reward, recompense, or compensation from what you give me, except love for my relatives. The commentators differed on the meaning of his statement: Except for the love of kinship. Some of them said: Its meaning is: Except that you love me for my kinship to you, and maintain the ties of kinship between me and you. It was mentioned that he said that: Abu Kurayb and Ya`qub told us, they said: Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives, he said: There was no clan of the Quraysh except that there was a kinship between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said: Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except that you love me for the kinship that is between me and you. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of `Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, on the authority of Tawus, regarding His statement: “Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward except the love of my relatives,” he said: Ibn `Abbas was asked about it, and Ibn Jubayr said: They are the relatives of the family of Muhammad. Ibn `Abbas said: You are hasty, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not have a clan of the Quraysh except that he had a kinship with them. He said: Then the verse: “Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward except the love of my relatives,” was revealed. He said: Except for the kinship that is between me and you, that you maintain it. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except the love of my relatives,” he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had relatives in all of Quraysh, and when they denied him and refused to pledge allegiance to him, he said: “O my people, if you refuse to pledge allegiance to me, then preserve my kinship among you, so that no one other than you from among the Arabs will be more deserving of my protection and support than you.” Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except the love of my relatives,” meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Quraysh 106:I do not ask of you anything from your wealth, but I ask you not to harm me because of the kinship between me and you, for you are my people and the ones who are most deserving of obeying me and responding to me. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the middleman among the Quraysh. He had relatives in every clan of the Quraysh. He said: ‘I do not ask of you for what I am calling you to except that you protect me in my kinship.’ Say: ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my kinship.’” Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was of intermediate lineage from the Quraysh. There was no tribe of the Quraysh who did not give birth to him. He said: Then God Almighty said: ‘Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives’: except that you love me for my kinship to you and protect me.” Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told us: Abthar told us: Hasin told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding this verse: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except the love of my relatives.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was from Banu Hashim, and his mother was from Banu Zuhrah, and his father’s mother was from Banu Makhzum. So he said: Protect me in my relatives. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Harmi told us: Shu’bah told us: ‘Amara told me, on the authority of ‘Ikrimah, regarding His statement: Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives.’ He said: You know my kinship, and you believe me in what I have brought, and you protect me. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward except love for my relatives.” And God, the Blessed and Exalted, commanded Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, not to ask people for this Qur’an for any reward except that they should maintain the kinship between him and them, and all the clans of Quraysh gave birth to him and there was kinship between him and them. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: except for the love of kinship is if you follow me, give me charity, and maintain the ties of kinship with me. Muhammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding His statement: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives,” he said: There was no clan of the Quraysh except that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a child among them, so he said: Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except that you love me for my kinship to you. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement: “Say: I do not ask of you for this any reward except love for my relatives,” meaning the Quraysh. He said: I am only a man from among you, so help me against my enemy and protect my relatives. As for that which I have brought to you, I do not ask of you any reward except love for my relatives, if you love me for my relatives and help me against my enemy. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives,” he said: He says: Except that you love me for my relatives as you love your relatives and maintain ties of kinship through them. What I have brought does not cut that off from me, so I do not seek for what I have brought any reward to take from you for that. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Saeed bin Abi Ayoub told me, on the authority of Ata bin Dinar, regarding his statement: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives,” meaning: I do not ask of you any reward for what I have brought you except that you love me for my relatives among you and protect me from the people. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: “Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward except love for my relatives,” he said: All of Quraysh had kinship between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said: Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward except that you love me for the sake of the kinship that is between me and you. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Say to those believers who follow you: I do not ask you for any reward for what I have brought you except that you love my relatives. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ismail bin Abaan told us, he said: Al-Sabah bin Yahya Al-Mari told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Al-Daylam, he said: When Ali bin Al-Hussein may God be pleased with him was brought as a prisoner and was made to stand on the stairs of Damascus, a man from the people of Ash-Sham stood up and said: Praise be to God who killed you and uprooted you, and cut off the approach of sedition. Ali bin Al-Hussein may God be pleased with him said to him: Have you recited the Qur’an? He said: Yes. He said: Have you recited Al-Ha Meem? He said: I recited the Qur’an but I did not recite Al-Ha Meem! He said: I did not recite Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives.’ He said: And you are they? He said: Yes. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Ismail narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Salam narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Ansar said: We did this and we did this, and it was as if they were boasting. Ibn Abbas, or al-Abbas - Abd al-Salam was uncertain - said: We have the advantage over you. report of that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he came to them in their gatherings and said: O group of Ansar, were you not humble and then God honored you through me? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Were you not astray and then God guided you through me? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Why don’t you answer me? They said: What should we say, O Messenger of God? He said: Why don’t you say: Didn’t your people expel you and we gave you shelter? Didn’t they deny you and we believed you? Didn’t they abandon you and we aided you? He kept saying that until they knelt on their knees and said: Our wealth and what is in our hands belong to God and His Messenger. He said: Then the verse was revealed: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love.” In the vicinity Yaqub told me, he said: Marwan told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Katheer, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives,” he said: It is the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad ibn Amara al-Asadi and Muhammad ibn Khalaf told me: Ubayd God told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I asked Amr ibn Shu`ayb about the words of God Almighty: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives.” He said: The relatives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Say, I do not ask of you, O people, any reward for what I have brought you except that you show affection to God and draw near to Him through righteous deeds and obedience. Mention of those who said that: Ali bin Dawud and his brother Muhammad bin Dawud also told me: Asim bin Ali told us: Qaza’ah bin Suwaid told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I do not ask of you any reward for what I have brought you of clear proofs and guidance except that you should be affectionate towards God and draw near to Him by obeying Him.” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur Ibn Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he said regarding this verse, Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives.’ He said: Relatives to God. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except the love of the relatives,” he said: Except for drawing closer to God, and showing affection to Him through righteous deeds. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan said, regarding His statement: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except the love of my relatives,” he said: I do not ask of you for what I have brought you, and for this book, any reward except the love of my relatives, except that you show affection to God by that which brings you closer to Him, and work in obedience to Him. He said: Bishr said: Yazid said: Yunus told me, on the authority of Al-Hasan, Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for the relatives” except that you show affection to God in that which brings you closer to Him. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: unless you maintain ties with your relatives. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Abu Amer told us, he said: Qurra told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Qasim, regarding his statement: Except for the love of relatives, he said: You were commanded to maintain ties of kinship. The first of the sayings on this matter is correct, and the one that most closely resembles the apparent meaning of the revelation, is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: Say, I do not ask you for any reward for it, O people of Quraysh, except that you love me for my kinship to you, and maintain the ties of kinship between me and you. Rather, I said that this interpretation is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse because of the inclusion of <in>in His statement, except for the love of my kinship. If the meaning of that were as stated by those who said, except that you love my kinship, or draw near to God, then the inclusion of <in>in the speech in this instance would not have had a known justification. The revelation would have been: except for the love of kinship, if what was meant by it was the command to love the kinship of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or except for the love of kinship, or except for the love of kinship, if what was meant by it was affection and drawing near. The inclusion of <in>in the speech is the clearest evidence that its meaning is: except for my love for my kinship to you, and that the definite article in affection was inserted in place of the addition, as was said, Indeed, Paradise is the abode (an-Nazi’at 79:41). His statement, except in this instance is an interrupted exception. The meaning of the speech is: Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it, but I ask you for the love of my kinship.’ Affection is in the accusative case in the sense that I mentioned. Some Basra grammarians said: It is in the accusative case because of an implied verb, meaning: unless I mention the affection of my kinship. And His statement: And whoever does a good deed - We will increase for him therein good, God Almighty says: And whoever does a good deed - that is, he does an act in which he obeys God among the believers - We will increase for him therein good, meaning: We multiply that good deed of his, so We give him ten in place of one, or whatever reward and recompense We will. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad told me, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding the statement of God Almighty: And whoever does a good deed, he said: He does a good deed. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And whoever does a good deed - We will increase for him good therein, he said: Whoever does good - We will increase for him good. Iqtiraaf means action. His saying: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Appreciative means: God is Forgiving of the sins of His servants, Appreciative of their good deeds and obedience to Him. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, God is Forgiving of sins, Appreciative of good deeds, multiplying them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Appreciative, he said: He forgave them their sins and thanked them for the blessings that He gave them and made them part of.
42:24: God Almighty says: Or do these polytheists say, Muhammad has fabricated a lie against God, and brought what he recites to us as an invention of his own? And His saying, If God wills, O Muhammad, He will seal your heart, so that you will forget this Qur’an that was revealed to you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Or do they say, ‘He has invented a lie against God?’ But if God wills, He will seal your heart, and He will make you forget the Qur’an. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: If God wills, He will seal your heart, he said: If God wills, He will make you forget what He has given you. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding the statement of God Almighty: If God wills, He will seal your heart, he said: He will imprint. And His statement: And God erases falsehood means: And God removes falsehood and obliterates it, and establishes the truth with His words that He revealed to you, O Muhammad, and establishes it. His saying: And God erases falsehood is in the nominative case as a subject, but the waw was deleted from it in the Qur’an, just as it was deleted in His saying: We will call the guards (al-Alaq 96:18), and in His saying: And He calls man to evil (al-Isra’ 17:11). It is not in the jussive mood in conjunction with He seals. And His statement: Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts, meaning that God Almighty says: Indeed, God is All-Knowing of what is in the breasts of His creation and what their hearts conceal. Nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him. He says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you were to invent a lie against God, I would seal your heart and take away what I have given you of My revelation, because I erase falsehood and eliminate it, and establish the truth. This is only God informing the disbelievers in Him, who claim that Muhammad invented this Qur’an on his own. So He informed them that if he did, He would do to him what He informed about in this verse.
42:25: God Almighty says: And God is the One who accepts the servant’s repentance when he returns to the Oneness of God and His obedience after his disbelief. And pardons the misdeeds. He says: And pardons that He punish him for his misdeeds and his sins from which he repented. And He knows what you do. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it as they do with a ya, meaning: And He knows what His servants do. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as you do with a ta, as a direct address. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, and they are close in meaning, so whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct. However, I like the ya’ more, because the speech before that was based on the report, and that is His statement, And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants, and what He, may He be glorified, means by His statement, And He knows what you do, is that your Lord knows, O people, what you do of good and evil, nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for all of that with His reward, so fear God in yourselves, and beware of doing that for which you will deserve punishment from Him. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir narrated to us, he said: Ishaq bin Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, on the authority of Hammam bin Al-Harith, he said: We came to Abdullah to ask him about this verse: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds and knows what you do. He said: So we found some people with him asking him about a man who had unlawfully committed adultery with a woman, then married her. So he recited this verse: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds and knows what you do.
42:26: God Almighty says: Those who believe in God and His Messenger, and do what God has commanded them to do, and refrain from what He has forbidden them, will respond to one another’s call. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Uthman told us, he said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Shaqiq bin Salamah, on the authority of Salamah bin Sabra, he said: Muadh addressed us and said: You are the believers, and you are the people of Paradise. By God, I hope that those whom you kill from among the Persians and Romans will enter Paradise, because if one of them does a deed for one of you, he says: You did well, may God have mercy on you. You did well, may God forgive you. Then he recited: And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds and increases them from His bounty. And His statement: And He will increase them from His bounty means, the Most High says: And He will increase those who believe and do righteous deeds, along with His answering their supplications and granting them what they ask for from His bounty over their asking of Him, by giving them what they did not ask for. And it was said: That bounty which the Most High has guaranteed that He will increase them is that He will allow them to intercede for their brothers’ brothers if they intercede for Him on behalf of their brothers, and they intercede for them. It was mentioned that he said that: Ubaidullah bin Muhammad Al-Faryabi told us, he said: Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Bashir, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, regarding the statement of God Almighty: And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be answered, he said: They will intercede for their brothers, and He will increase them from His bounty, he said: They will intercede for the brothers of their brothers. And His saying: And for the disbelievers is a severe punishment. God Almighty says: And for the disbelievers in God, on the Day of Resurrection, is a severe punishment for their disbelief in Him. The Arab scholars differed over the meaning of His statement, And those who believe respond. Some of them said: It means that He responded, making them the doers. Thus, those in His statement is in the nominative case, and the action belongs to them. The interpretation of the statement according to this school of thought is: And those who believe and do righteous deeds responded to their Lord by believing in Him and working in obedience to Him when He called them to that. Another of them said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And He answers those who believe. This statement has two possible interpretations: One is the nominative case, meaning: And God answers those who believe. The other is what was said by the one who said the statement we mentioned. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said, And those who believe respond, the word those who would be in the accusative case meaning, And God responds to those who believe. It was stated in the Qur'an, So their Lord responded to them 3:195, meaning, So their Lord responded to them. However, when you say responded, you insert the lam into the object, and when you say answered, you delete the lam, and responded to them would mean, He responded to them, as God, the Most High, said, And when they measure to them or weigh to them Al-Mutaffifin 73:3. The meaning, and God knows best, is, And when they measure to them or weigh to them, they lose. Al-Mutaffifin 73:3. He said, And the word those who" would be in the nominative case, so that the action is made for them, meaning, those who believe respond to God, and He increases their response, and belief in Him is from His grace. We have already explained the correct interpretation of this statement based on what Mu'adh and those we have mentioned have said about it.
42:27: It was mentioned that this verse was revealed for the sake of a group of needy Muslims who wished for the spaciousness of this world and wealth. So God Almighty said: And if God were to expand the provision for His servants, and make it abundant and plentiful with Him, they would transgress and exceed the limit that God has set for them to something other than what He has set for them in His lands by riding on the earth what He has forbidden them. But He sends down their provision in an amount to suffice them as He wills from it. Mention of those who said that: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abu Hani’ said: I heard Amr ibn Harith and others saying: This verse was revealed about the people of the Suffa, And if God were to extend provision to His servants, they would transgress upon the earth, but He sends down in due measure as He wills. That is because they said: If only we had, so they wished. Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us: Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Maqri told us: Haywa told us: Abu Hani’ told me that he heard Amr bin Harith say: This verse was revealed, and then he mentioned something similar. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And if God were to expand the provision for His servants, they would transgress on the earth the verse... He said: It was said: The best provision is that which does not make you arrogant or distract you. “It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘What I fear most for my nation is the splendor and abundance of this world.’ Someone said to him: ‘O Prophet of God, does good bring evil?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Does good bring evil?’ Then God revealed a verse to him, and whenever a verse was revealed to him, he would be distressed by it and his face would turn red. When the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, felt better, he said: ‘Does good bring evil?’ He would say it three times: ‘Good only brings good.’ He would say it three times. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would speak oddly, but by God, he never spoke except that he was frustrated or hurt. As for a servant whom God has given wealth, and he spends it in the way of God, which He has made obligatory and which He is pleased with, that is a servant for whom good is intended and for whom he has resolved to do good. As for a servant whom God has given wealth, and he spends it in his desires and pleasures, and turns away from the right of God over him, that is a servant for whom evil is intended and for whom evil is resolved.” And His saying: He is All-Knowing and All-Seeing of His servants. God Almighty says: God is All-Knowing and All-Seeing of what is good for His servants and what is bad for them, whether they are rich or poor, wealthy or poor, and other things that are good for them or bad for them. He is All-Knowing and All-Seeing of their management and their disposal of what is good for them.
42:28: God Almighty says: And it is God who sends down rain from the sky and helps you with it, O people, after they have despaired meaning: after they have despaired of its descent and coming and spreads His mercy meaning: and spreads His mercy among His creation, and by mercy He means the rain that He sends down from the sky. And in a similar manner to what we said, the people of interpretation said. Mention of those who said that: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that it was said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: The land has become barren, and the people have despaired. He said: Then they will have rain. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, he said: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: After they had despaired, he said: They had lost hope. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that a man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and said: O Commander of the Faithful, the rain has been scarce and the people have despaired. He said: You have been given rain. And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired and spreads His mercy. And His statement: And He is the Guardian, the Praiseworthy, meaning: He is the One who is with you through His goodness and grace, the Praiseworthy for His favor to you and His blessings upon you in His creation.
42:29: God Almighty says: And among His proofs against you, O people, is that He is able to revive you after your annihilation, and raise you from your graves after your affliction, He created the heavens and the earth and whatever creatures He dispersed throughout them meaning whatever creatures He dispersed throughout the heavens and the earth. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And what He has dispersed throughout them of creatures, he said: people and angels. And He is Able to gather them together if He wills, he said: And He is Able to gather what He has dispersed throughout them of creatures if He wills to gather them. He has power that is not difficult for Him, just as it was not difficult for Him to create and disperse them. God Almighty says: Thus He is Able to gather His creation by gathering them on the Day of Resurrection after their parts have been scattered in the graves.
42:30: God Almighty says: Whatever misfortune befalls you, O people, in this world in yourselves, your families, or your wealth, is because of what your hands have earned. He says: This only befalls you as a punishment from God for the sins you committed between you and your Lord. Your Lord forgives you for many of your crimes, so He does not punish you for them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of those who said that: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ayoub told us, he said: I read in the book of Abu Qilabah, he said: “The verse, ‘So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it’ was revealed while Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him was eating, so he stopped and said: ‘O Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), will I see what I have done of good or evil?’ He said: ‘Do you think that what you have seen that you dislike is from the atom’s weight of evil, and the atom’s weight of good is stored up for you to be given on the Day of Resurrection?’” Abu Idris said: “I see its proof in the Book of God, He said: ‘And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned.
